items.title: Live: US military launches another wave of strikes on Iran
items.description: The US military says it has fired a fresh series of strikes against Iran to "degrade their ability to threaten freedom of navigation" in the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Australians face record high rents as agents see 'inquiries flooding in'
items.description: Rents are soaring in several capital cities as low vacancy rates collide with rising interest rates and population growth.

items.title: Trump calls Iran 'scum' and Ukraine gets big win on wild day at NATO
items.description: Donald Trump says his country will probably continue to attack Iran and says Ukraine will be given permission to manufacture much-needed Patriot missiles as it fights Russia's full-scale invasion.

items.title: 'Shouldn't occur': Change demanded after Telstra outage
items.description: Advocates have demanded changes to how telecommunication companies are regulated and held accountable for outages after Telstra became the latest telco to suffer a large-scale network failure.

items.title: Here's how the Telstra outage impacted these Australians
items.description: Millions have potentially been impacted by the Telstra outage. Here's how it affected Australians doing basic everyday things, from making calls to measuring blood sugar levels.

items.title: New South Wales writes a new fate in blood after epic decider
items.description: Against all odds and with most of their state doubting them, Laurie Daley's New South Wales side has pulled off one of the greatest wins in Blues history.

items.title: The UK's next PM has a carefully curated image. Not everyone is buying it
items.description: For some, Andy Burnham's casual communication style is refreshing. Others say it's a carefully crafted facade, disguising the fact that he's a ruthless Labour Party lifer.

items.title: Modi met with support and human rights protests as he arrives in Melbourne
items.description: A large swathe of the Indian diaspora wants to warmly welcome Narendra Modi to Melbourne, but others demand Australia put pressure on him over his human rights record.

items.title: As snowfall declines, a key ingredient is keeping the ski season alive
items.description: Data shows snow depth has been declining in Australia since the 1950s, with resorts turning to snowmaking to guarantee a strong ski season.

items.title: 'Twenty minutes or so': The blunt warning of China's nuclear capability
items.description: Victor Gao, the vice-president of a major Chinese think tank, conducts some sabre-rattling in the wake of China's missile test in the Pacific.

items.title: 'Profound injustice': Last woman executed in UK pardoned by king
items.description: The case of Ruth Ellis has gripped Britain for decades and inspired the 1985 film Dance with a Stranger.

items.title: ABC rejects claims of antisemitic bias ahead of fronting royal commission
items.description: The ABC and SBS will face questioning over complaints of bias and antisemitism when executives appear at the royal commission on Thursday.

items.title: Racist commentary called out in World Cup coverage
items.description: Leading experts say racial stereotypes in World Cup coverage can be damaging for athletes' leadership aspirations and have an impact on Black communities more broadly.

items.title: Cost-of-living crisis 'hits from two directions' as major musicals close
items.description: As two more major musicals bite the dust, the local theatre industry hopes a live performance incentive modelled on a successful UK scheme will provide salvation.

items.title: Emmy nominations 2026 revealed, with The Pitt and Hacks topping list
items.description: The Pitt takes the lead as the most nominated series for the 78th annual Primetime Emmy Awards, with Hacks in second place.

items.title: TV catchphrase quiz: Guess the show from the famous quote
items.description: Now for the story of 20 famous TV quotes, and the one quiz that had no choice but to keep them all together.

items.title: New varieties set Australian coffee industry up for expansion
items.description: Australians are among the world's biggest coffee drinkers but less than 1 per cent of the coffee consumed nationwide is grown locally. That could be about to change.

items.title: Hobart 'Stadium 2.0' developer's company in liquidation, as he works on new waterfront project
items.description: Tasmanian developer Dean Coleman's company, which was involved in the rejected 'Stadium 2.0' plan for Hobart, is in liquidation. He's now involved in a separate development proposal at Regatta Point.

items.title: Police investigate two suspicious Melbourne house fires
items.description: The two house fires started within minutes of each other, less than two kilometres apart in Melbourne's north.

items.title: Queensland on track for another record year of motorcycle crashes
items.description: Police say they've seen a rise in anti-social hooning behaviour as Queensland records a rise in fatal motorcycle crashes.

items.title: Melbourne injecting room cut ambulance callouts by 70pc, report reveals
items.description: Data from a new paper shows the number of heroin-related ambulance call-outs dropped from 48 a month to 14 a month in the first five years following the Richmond medically supervised injecting room's opening.

items.title: Aboriginal activist tells court of obligation to prevent 'slaughtered' forests
items.description: An Aboriginal activist has told a Tasmanian court she has a cultural obligation to "protect lands that are being slaughtered", after she was charged with trespassing while protesting in a logging coupe.

items.title: Dozens of Aboriginal language custodians call for further revival efforts
items.description: Aboriginal language custodians release a road map for the survival and revival of Northern Territory Indigenous languages.

items.title: Adelaide employer to pay $25k penalty for not providing adequate meal breaks
items.description: An automotive industry group made threats "to create fear" in a man who had brought legal action against his employer for not giving him adequate lunch breaks, a tribunal judgement has found.

items.title: Fears towns will be 'decimated' as rice miller cuts production
items.description: Communities in southern NSW fear large cutbacks to rice processing could put hundreds of people out of work and decimate regional economies.
